chapter: Tiger Rag and Mopah Blues explained
title: The Mopah Blues lawsuit over Livery Stable Blues
summary: He says Livery Stable Blues echoed an older tune, that they won the royalty suit, and plays the Mopah Blues.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Now if there's any man living that knows anything about the Mopah Blues, which was played in New Orleans ten years before I went to Chicago, they'll attest to this tune when they hear it. With the exception of the introduction and the runs. The runs were made purposely so whoever on this tune could cry to sound something like the Liverstable Blues. Now we won the suit, we got the royalties from the Liverstable Blues, from the Victor people, and we are next to peace which I'm sorry to say that I didn't want. But Mr. Boyk had told me go ahead, that's the only way we can show the court now. If the man come forward and claim this peace, then all that money that we had put out would have to be rescinded to us. Now here it is here. Now this court is my own adding to it. It had nothing new with the Mopah Blues. Now this is the Mopah Blues. Now this is the Mopah Blues. Now this is the Mopah Blues. Now this is the Mopah Blues. Now this is the Mopah Blues. Now the Indian didn't go like this. It went something like the Mopah Blues. This was not into their thing. This I added to make them cry. I added to make them cry. I added to make them cry. The Mopah Blues. Thank you. And they find out about it, they'll think that I've lied all the way through. That's why I give you this, for your take. I'd like to bring you up to the time that we went to London. After Robinson joined the band, we boarded the steamship.
